page: UpCloud GPU-48xCPU-480GB-2xB200 is a KVM-hypervised GPU server configured with 48 Intel Xeon 8570 physical cores running at 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system features 480.0 GB of RAM, providing 10.0 GB of memory per core. Acceleration is driven by two NVIDIA Blackwell B200 GPUs delivering a combined 384 GB of VRAM. No local storage is bundled with this instance type, and it includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier performance in multi-threaded and specialized workloads. The PassMark CPU score of 88,533.65 and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression speed of 706.88 GB/sec rank in the top tier. Memory bandwidth for large uncached blocks is also top-tier at 385.14 GB/sec. For AI workloads, the instance achieves a top-tier prompt processing speed of 9,458.91 tokens/sec using a small 135M LLM model, alongside a strong text generation speed of 317.76 tokens/sec. Single-core performance is moderate, with stress-ng single-core scoring in the average tier.

This server offers high resource density for memory-bound and GPU-accelerated tasks, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for large-scale parallel processing despite the shared CPU allocation. The primary hardware tradeoff is the complete absence of local storage, requiring external storage attachments. This configuration is suited for large language model inference, deep learning training, high-performance database operations, and complex physics simulations.
